unsure: The tree checker failing at tailcalls on the base build ('Tree has erroneous type: x()') suggests the real defect is upstream: after fields, trees still carry the singleton type of what is now a method (x.type with x a lazy accessor), and any retyping fails on it. A fix in fields that widens those types when it turns a local lazy val into an accessor would be more principled and would also satisfy the checker; this change fixes only the retyping in Duplicators, which is where users hit it. The widening applies to SingleType(_, sym) with sym lazy, a method and local to a block, which after fields is exactly a local lazy accessor.
note: Duplicators.fixType widens the singleton type of a local lazy accessor to its underlying type, so the duplicated lifted lambda's declared result type matches the retyped call.
